title: The futility of false doctrines and the diminishing of truth
english: It is so; no longer is the rider a rider. And the truths began to act, because they had been diminished. [Gapped] by [Gapped] way [Gapped] history. For if the 'belly' and its 'foods' are 'nullified', when [Gapped] life [Gapped] and the world [Gapped] the [Gapped] 'the truths began to act' [Gapped] not being the 'truth-telling ones' [Gapped] that they are not of God.

He indeed says in Jeremiah to the false prophets who mix the logical [things] with 'chaff'; if the 'chaff' is 'grain' to the wind—'the Lord says, are my words not like grain?' (Jeremiah 23:28)—the 'words of grain' are those of God. Those able to divide them and to refine and to prepare, these are 'truth-telling' or 'truths', so that I may speak femininely according to the word. Those dividing ecclesiastically the 'words' of God, being 'grain', make nourishing breads and bring 'fine flour' to the altar; for there are also sacrifices offered through 'fine flour'. Those from the heterodox, not dividing the 'words' of God as is necessary, but dividing them errantly and unto impiety, 'truth-tell' badly. The 'flour' of these is 'rejected', serving neither for sacrifice nor for food.

In Hosea, therefore, he says to the prophet: 'Why have you passed over impiety, and endured its iniquities, and eaten false fruit?' (Hosea 8:7). Then he says: 'You have sown corruption with the wind, and this destruction; a whirlwind had no strength to make flour' (Hosea 8:7). This is badly 'hidden' from the 'truth-telling [one]'. In the same way also concerning the intelligible [things] and [Gapped] in the Gospel [Gapped] 'to be two in the field, one being taken and one being left' (Matthew 24:40); and 'two being truths, one is taken [Gapped] it is left' [Gapped]; these are those who sow [Gapped] [Gapped] with them [Gapped] having been given.

They sow [something] and from it they 'forgive' again, 'receiving' by the same scripture, and it 'is forgiven' as 'I have sown without fruit' toward someone. Not 'leaven' [is it], not 'leaven' true, not the 'leaven' which is able to be produced and to be brought forward as a sacrifice.

Concerning this futility, in Isaiah it says: 'If you bring spelt, it is in vain; a memorial in vain is to me' (Isaiah 55:13). Nor does the 'memorial' have the 'fragrance' of 'incense'; therefore 'it is an abomination.' Nor does the 'spelt' have anything useful for being made into bread or to be brought forward as a sacrifice; therefore 'it is in vain.'

These then, the 'truths' which are praiseworthy, have 'diminished'; for they no longer clarify the scriptures, since the space has been collapsed, having reached the end of this age. The 'truths' therefore 'diminished, because they were made few'; as much as is upon you, you have made them 'few,' you have constructed them weakly.

Moreover, is it not because of this, as the time no longer permits, that they do not 'be true'?—to the extent that they have been diminished for these [people]; do not diminish the 'fewness' here in terms of number, but of their power and strength. But has their strength become [less] beyond the time? For you think that as far as possible these 'truths' do not 'be true' even after this, for those able to be nourished by them.

They 'were made few,' because the greater part of those being nourished was diminished and fell away from seeking such nourishment. Moreover, do we not also receive this inappropriately there, with 'and the sun was darkened' (Matthew 27:45)?—and concerning the 'light' and the 'sun' let us say that, although it seemed to 'be darkened' regarding those, they 'were not darkened.' Again, therefore, I say as toward these men...
